L381@P4: Intuitively, a deformation of the determinant hypersurface, subject to the condition that its
L382@P4: dual remains of dimension 2n − 2, should have a deformation of the Segre as its dual variety.
L383@P4: But the Segre is rigid, its only deformations in PW∗ are translates by projective automorphisms.
L384@P4: Hence the only deformations of the determinant hypersurface, with duals of the same dimension,
L385@P4: should be translates by projective automorphisms as well.
L386@P4: The problem with this intuitive argument is that the dual map can be highly discontinuous,
L387@P4: especially in the presence of singularities, and the determinant hypersurface is very singular.
L388@P4: Nevertheless, the conclusion turns out to be correct:
L389@P4: Every small deformation of the determinant hypersurface, with dual variety of the same dimension, is a translate by a projective automorphism.
